alternate_names: Devi Talab Temple, Jalandhar (the actual temple of this name - see note)
deities: Mata Tripurmalini (goddess Durga; the temple is counted among the 51 Shakti Peethas - the site where Sati's right breast is believed to have fallen)
Kali (shrine adjacent to the main sanctum)
Lord Shiva (seated statue in the centre of the talab, with water spouting like a fountain)
Shiva lingam in the replica Amarnath Cave; figurines and paintings of many Hindu deities
festivals: Shri Harballabh Sangeet Sammelan (annual classical music festival in December; one of India's oldest, since 1875; Ravi Shankar performed here in 1977)

history.period: About 200 years old (per Expedia - verify); the talab itself is described as ancient
history.summary: CRITICAL CSV FLAG: this record is almost certainly a CSV ERROR or DUPLICATE of row 819 ('Shri Devi Talab Mandir', Jalandhar). Every source found places the famous Devi Talab Mandir in JALANDHAR (Tanda Road), not Ludhiana - about 55 km away. The only 'Devi Talab Mandir / Ludhiana' listing found is a clearly miscategorised directory page (datagemba) whose own address is in Jalandhar. No separate Devi Talab Mandir in Ludhiana could be verified. The dataset owner should merge this row with 819 or remove it. About the actual temple (for reference): the Devi Talab Mandir is a 51-Shakti-Peetha shrine to Mata Tripurmalini, set around a large talab (sacred tank) with a seated Shiva statue at its centre; the complex includes an Amarnath Cave replica, a Kali shrine, a mock mountain with giant deities, and a charitable hospital on Mandir Marg. The temple's prabandhak committee uses an eco-friendly treatment (OXIBON) to keep the ancient pond's water clean.

name: Devi Talab Mandir
town: Ludhiana (CSV - UNVERIFIED; the actual temple of this name is in Jalandhar)
town_description: Note: the famous Devi Talab Mandir is in Jalandhar, on Tanda Road about 1 km from Jalandhar City railway station - NOT in Ludhiana. Jalandhar is one of Punjab's oldest cities, historically linked to the Indus Valley Civilization, and a noted centre of the Shakta tradition.

travel.airport: Sri Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport, Amritsar (about 80 km from Jalandhar); Ludhiana's Sahnewal airport has limited service (verify).
travel.railway: Jalandhar City railway station on the Delhi-Amritsar line is about 1 km from the temple.
travel.road: Jalandhar is on NH-44; Ludhiana is about 60 km away by road. The temple is on Tanda Road in the city.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for weather; December for the Harballabh Sangeet Sammelan; Navratri for festivals.
visitor_information.opening_hours: The Jalandhar temple is listed as open 5:00 AM to 10:00 PM daily (verify). No hours apply to a Ludhiana shrine under this name, which could not be verified to exist.
